name: normal
interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm at approximately 75 bpm with a normal axis and narrow QRS complexes. P waves are upright in lead II and precede each QRS. R-wave progression across the precordial leads is normal and there is no significant ST-segment elevation or depression. This appears to be a normal ECG.
reference:
Findings:
Regular rhythm with normal P waves preceding each QRS.

Impression:
Normal ECG. No acute abnormality.

name: afib
interpretation: Broad-complex rhythm with a left bundle branch block morphology — a wide QRS with a dominant negative deflection in V1-V3 and notched complexes laterally. Discrete P waves are difficult to identify and the rhythm looks somewhat irregular, so atrial fibrillation with underlying LBBB cannot be excluded. Clinical correlation is advised.
reference:
Findings:
Irregularly irregular rhythm without discernible P waves. Broad QRS with a monophasic R wave in the lateral leads and absent septal Q waves.

Impression:
Findings consistent with atrial fibrillation. Complete left bundle branch block. No acute ischemic changes identified.

name: inferior_mi
interpretation: Sinus rhythm at a normal rate. The inferior leads (III and aVF) are low in amplitude with small Q waves in lead III. These changes are subtle and may be positional, but an old inferior wall myocardial infarction cannot be entirely excluded. No acute ST-segment elevation is seen.
reference:
Findings:
Regular rhythm with normal P waves preceding each QRS. Abnormal QRS morphology. Pathological Q waves in the inferior (II, III, and aVF) leads.

Impression:
Findings consistent with sinus rhythm. Inferior myocardial infarction.

name: anteroseptal_mi
interpretation: Sinus rhythm. There is poor R-wave progression across the anterior precordial leads with QS-type complexes in V1-V2 and a delayed transition. This pattern can be seen with an old anteroseptal infarction, though lead placement or body habitus could produce a similar appearance.
reference:
Findings:
Regular rhythm with normal P waves preceding each QRS. Abnormal QRS morphology. Pathological Q waves in the anteroseptal (V1, V2, and V3) leads.

Impression:
Findings consistent with sinus rhythm. Anteroseptal myocardial infarction.

name: lvh
interpretation: Sinus rhythm with markedly increased QRS voltages in the precordial leads, meeting voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. There are associated downsloping ST-segment and T-wave changes in the lateral and inferior leads, consistent with LV strain or ischemia.
reference:
Findings:
Regular rhythm with normal P waves preceding each QRS. Broad, notched P waves. Increased left-sided QRS voltage meeting hypertrophy criteria. Ischemic-type repolarization changes.

Impression:
Findings consistent with sinus rhythm. Left atrial enlargement. Left ventricular hypertrophy. Non-specific ischemia.

name: rbbb
interpretation: Sinus rhythm with a broad QRS. Lead V1 shows an rSR' ('rabbit-ear') pattern and there are wide slurred S waves in the lateral leads — complete right bundle branch block. The frontal-plane axis is markedly leftward with an rS pattern in the inferior leads, suggesting a co-existing left anterior fascicular block (bifascicular block).
reference:
Findings:
Regular rhythm with normal P waves preceding each QRS. Broad QRS with an rSR' pattern in V1 and wide S waves laterally. Left axis deviation with small q in aVL and rS in the inferior leads.

Impression:
Findings consistent with sinus rhythm. Complete right bundle branch block. Left anterior fascicular block. No acute ischemic changes identified.
